title: The Lead agent's turn says it is thinking from start to end, so the page holds the person's next message instead of a refused send
request: The owner pasted the server's log: POST /api/drafts/{id}/messages answered 409 Conflict twice and POST /api/drafts/{id}/team once, and called them bugs and conflicts.
spec: While an agent turn holds a draft, the page shows it is working, keeps the person's words in the box instead of posting them, and keeps the team walk from starting; the server's refusal, when it still happens, is said calmly. Every Lead agent turn reports thinking at its start and not thinking at its end, after a reply, a silent end or an error.
plan: Read which routes answer 409 and why: the draft's turn lock, held while an agent answers.
Read the draft's record in the development database: the person's question at 19:39:58 was answered at 19:41:24, after six model calls, and the 409s came in between.
Find why the page allowed sending: the Lead agent's turns never emitted a thinking status, so the page never knew a turn was running.
Write a failing test, fix the turn at its entry, and harden the page: hold sends and the team walk while thinking, set thinking as soon as a message is accepted, and say a 409 calmly.

decisions.decision: Fix the status at the Lead agent turn's single entry with try/finally.
decisions.why: Every path through the turn (a reply, a dashboard, a refused build, a silent turn, an exception) passes through _run; one place cannot forget a path.

decisions.decision: Keep the server's 409 as it is.
decisions.why: The turn lock is right: two turns on one draft would interleave the conversation. The defect was the page not knowing a turn was running.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/case_home.py (_run says thinking, runs _turn, and always says it ended); dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/views/home.html (send holds the words while thinking, sets thinking once a message is accepted, a 409 is said calmly; the team step waits while thinking); tests/test_case_home.py (a reply, a silent turn and an error each start and end the thinking status).

findings.defect: Messages and the team walk were refused with 409 while the Lead agent answered.
findings.scenario: Ask 'which gender churn more?' on a Telco table; the turn runs about 90 seconds; send another message or press Walk with the team meanwhile: both are refused and the page shows an error.
findings.cause: The Lead agent's turn (case_home) emitted no thinking status at its start and only on a RuntimeError at its end, so the page's busy state stayed off.
findings.fix: The turn says thinking at its start and not thinking in a finally block; the page also sets thinking when a message is accepted and holds sends and the team walk while thinking.
findings.test: test_a_turn_says_it_is_thinking_and_always_says_when_it_ends fails before the fix and passes after.

measurements.name: the Lead agent's tests
measurements.gate: all pass with the new test
measurements.result: test_case_home, test_case_agent, test_lead_bounded_choice and test_no_data_solution pass, 200 tests.
limits: Scripted models; how long a live turn takes is not changed by this fix.

outcome: While the Lead agent answers, the page shows it, holds the next message in the box and keeps the team walk waiting; the server no longer has to refuse them.
lessons: A lock on the server needs its state on the page: an agent path that does not report it makes the lock look like a bug.
Put the start and end of a long operation at its single entry, in try/finally, so no path forgets the end.
Read the record before guessing: the turn was slow, not stuck, and the timestamps said so.
risks: The Lead agent's turns are still slow on a simple question (six model calls); that is a separate change.
